chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Consider whom you breastfeed your children with, for the child grows upon it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: Why is the choice of wet nurse important in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia emphasis on *tarbiyah* (upbringing) and the profound influence of early environmental factors on a child's moral and physical development. It reflects the broader scholarly understanding that wet nursing was not merely a biological necessity but a key determinant in lineage and character formation, often cited in discussions of *radāʿah* (milk kinship). The advice underscores the responsibility of parents to choose a nurse whose piety and temperament align with their desired upbringing for the child.
